lines.trans: Did Cindy really just smile right now?
Not a smirk, just a bright genuine smile, right?
Later when the concert starts, once the cue sign goes out, the lift will rise onto the stage for your entrance.
I know how stage lifts work.
Is it supposed to wobble like this? On the outside it looks pretty rickety.
Stage lifts always wobble like this.
Then that is a relief—so this is how it rises up!
A producer is supposed to protect the performer, yet you look way more scared than I am!
I am not all that scared, really.
If you are not scared, how about letting go of my arm first?

words.gloss: let go of, why don't you?

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

examples.text: 비웃은 것도 아니고 그냥 해맑게 웃은 거 맞지?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

examples.text: 백승찬은 해맑은 데가 있어서 호감일 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.

meanings.note: Bound noun (Sino-Korean 位) paired with Sino-Korean numerals to express ranking (일 위 'first place', 이 위 'second place').

examples.text: 이번 주 차트 일 위 곡이에요.
examples.trans: It's this week's number-one chart song.

examples.trans: Is that really so?

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave
